records.trigger: Developing, generating, verifying, or repairing a HAMR SysML system targeting Rust on Microkit, especially when generation reports that the configured frame cannot accommodate the used scheduling budget.
records.principle: Carry one traceable set of behavioral, interface, state, and timing obligations through modeling, type checking, scheduling feasibility review, generation, implementation, proof, testing, and repair. Stop dependent work at a failed gate; repair the owning artifact or environment without weakening the obligations. Detecting infeasibility early prevents wasted work but does not establish engineering acceptance.
records.semantic_choice: Translate conditional requirements into guarded obligations over dispatch-frozen inputs and explicit pre-state. Preserve conjunction, disjunction, strict versus inclusive boundaries, initialization, hysteresis memory, and latched failure semantics. Treat an output-dependent condition as a guarantee implication, as in REQ_MMI_6, rather than an environmental assumption. Treat timing diagnostics as feasibility failures, not permission to relax required timing.
records.structural_placement: The model owner maintains the System, Process wrappers, typed ports, connections, thread attributes, GUMBO contracts, and requirement traces. Each Microkit Process contains one Thread; preserve the supplied flat Monitor topology and every existing source interface. Thread behavior belongs in its GUMBO block and developer-owned Rust entry-point bodies. HAMR owns generated bridges, APIs, GUMBOX functions, build infrastructure, and marked generated regions. The schedule owner maintains the editable schedule with justified allocations; proof and test owners check the same model revision and generated contracts.
records.repair_gate: Input: the failing stage, exact diagnostics, configuration, model and generated-artifact revisions, preserved obligations, and an artifact diff. Output: a classified cause, a requirement-preserving repair proposal, and rerun results or an explicit unresolved blocker. For a frame-budget failure, reconcile the reported budget with actual allocations, required execution allowances and tool-accounted overhead; do not assume what any term means. Repair demonstrable configuration or allocation errors, or justify an implementation/scheduling change using established timing evidence. Do not invent execution-time bounds, shrink budgets without support, increase a required frame, remove a component, or weaken contracts to obtain a green gate. Restart at the earliest affected stage and rerun all invalidated downstream gates. If no supported feasible repair is available, retain the failure and report infeasibility.
prerequisites: A selected System, complete project and compatible HAMR/AADL library source paths, resolved data types, and explicit Microkit/Rust generation configuration.
A baseline of all source interfaces, connections, dispatch protocols, periods, domains, behavioral clauses, and required platform timing constraints.
Known temperature representation, units, arithmetic semantics, and admissible ranges; the supplied Monitor excerpt imports but does not define its data model.
Explicit initialization and update semantics for lastCmd and lastMonitorMode; declarations alone do not establish previous-dispatch semantics.
An authoritative distinction between required frame/period constraints and adjustable configuration, with justified scheduling budgets and consistent units.
A compatible Sireum installation and the documented CLI operations; any MCP wrapper must be separately established as usable.
cargo and cargo-verus availability for their respective stages, generated Rust targets including aarch64-unknown-none where requested, and MICROKIT_SDK/MICROKIT_BOARD for top-level Microkit builds.

Resolution of behavior gaps before claiming full-system conformance: the supplied failure detector has no GUMBO behavior, and the mode-case description mentions timeout without an encoded timer or timeout guard.
exclusions: No inference of execution-time bounds, diagnostic time units, or the composition of the reported used budget.
No inference that the supplied Monitor example caused the recorded frame-budget failure.
No assumption that code generation, component tests, or verification of selected contracts establishes whole-system timing or deployment correctness.
No EventDataPort Option/Some/None compute-contract syntax; the supplied modeling guidance reports that syntax unsupported.
No transfer of Microkit-specific structural and build obligations to other targets without separate support.

preserved_obligations: Stage G1 — Requirements and modeling. Input: supplied requirements, model, type definitions, and R. Output: a clause-to-owner trace, typed architecture and GUMBO contracts, state-transition interpretation, timing constraints, and unresolved questions. Gate: retain every source interface and requirement; expose missing semantics rather than supplying unsupported behavior.

Stage G2 — Type checking. Input: edited model and compatible complete source paths. Output: HAMR type-check diagnostics. Gate: resolve model errors before generation; after every model edit repeat checking. Missing core types call for sourcepath repair; unsupported constructs inside bundled AADL libraries call for version alignment rather than arbitrary project-model changes.

Stage G3 — Scheduling feasibility screening. Input: required frame/period constraints, editable schedule, configuration, and justified budgets. Output: a reconciled capacity calculation or explicit missing-accounting blocker. Gate: B <= F is a necessary capacity condition, not sufficient schedulability evidence. Preserve required timing, ordering, and domains. Early screening may prevent wasted generation; generator accounting remains authoritative for its own acceptance check.

Stage G4 — Generation. Input: type-checked model, selected System, generation configuration, and scheduling review. Output: generated Microkit infrastructure, Rust skeletons, contracts, APIs, tests, and diagnostics. Gate: a nonzero generation result blocks use of incomplete output as an accepted baseline. Use an isolated temporary output directory for diagnostic generation experiments and review regeneration diffs and ownership markers.

Stage G5 — Implementation. Input: generated signatures/contracts and R. Output: application logic inside verus! blocks and developer-owned regions. Gate: initialize every output DataPort without reading inputs; initialize and maintain local state; compute from frozen inputs using generated get_/put_ APIs; retain read-compute-write semantics. lastCmd and lastMonitorMode must represent the intended prior dispatch and be updated consistently after computing the new result.

Stage G6 — Proof. Input: model contracts, generated Verus contracts, implementation, and declared assumptions. Output: model-level Logika and implementation-level Verus diagnostics with scope and trusted-body boundaries. Gate: resolve relevant obligations and check assumption satisfiability; model checking cannot substitute for Rust proof. Output integration guarantees constrain put_ callers and input assumptions constrain get_ results. Do not hide core control logic behind external_body to silence failures; record any genuinely trusted helper boundary.

Stage G7 — Testing. Input: generated test infrastructure, requirement-derived expected behavior, implementation, and state setup. Output: serial manual assertions, GUMBOX boundary cases, state-aware harness cases, PropTest outcomes, and retained counterexamples. Gate: all tests use serial isolation; initialization, valid/invalid statuses, all modes, exact alarm and hysteresis boundaries, both prior command values, state sequences, and relevant type extremes are exercised. Use testComputeCBwGSV for contract state and explicit multi-dispatch tests for state evolution. RejectedPrecondition is a rejection, not a passing behavioral case; inspect rejection rates and valid-case coverage.

Stage G8 — Integration and acceptance review. Input: consistent model/generated/code revisions, proof/test results, generated build files, and justified schedule. Output: build diagnostics and a scoped obligation-coverage report. Gate: separately resolve system timing and integration obligations, preserve connection-driven composition, and report unsupported failure-detection or timeout behavior as incomplete. Generation success alone is not acceptance.

Stage G9 — Repair. Input: any failed gate and its reproducible diagnostic context. Output: an ownership-correct repair and regression checks. Gate: preserve R, retain counterexamples, and repeat every affected upstream and downstream check without editing generated contracts or infrastructure to conceal the defect.

Restore introduced interface drift to the source baseline; if an existing source interface itself cannot be processed, record the unresolved compatibility blocker instead of rewriting it or deleting obligations. records.trigger: A requirement assigns an interface component responsibility for reporting failure when any member of an explicitly identified input group is invalid, clearing failure when all are valid, and copying corresponding payloads when no interface failure exists.

records.semantic_choice: Translate 'any invalid' as disjunction, 'both/all valid' as conjunction, and 'if no interface failure then copy' as a one-way implication. Status validity is distinct from numeric range membership and from a Boolean payload expressing operational usability.
records.structural_placement: Attach the behavioral contract to the thread that owns the failure and copied outputs, as Manage_Monitor_Interface_i does. Preserve process forwarding and system connections. Consumers retain ownership of their existing reactions to failure; do not move mode selection or actuation into the interface thread.

Do not weaken assumptions to exclude invalid inputs or introduce output guarantees for unspecified failure branches. These checks have not been implemented or performed.
prerequisites: The target has explicit requirements for the same three obligations: any-invalid failure, all-valid nonfailure, and conditional payload copying.

The responsible component can observe the grouped statuses and payloads within a defined invocation snapshot.

exclusions: Do not infer validity from numeric bounds, resolution, or physical plausibility.
Do not include unrelated inputs merely because they also carry status fields; current_tempWstatus is not in the monitor alarm-range validity group.
Do not infer hold, reset, suppression, or default payload behavior when failure is true.
Do not derive autopilot control logic from this rule: the provided autopilot excerpt distinguishes status from Guidance Valid but does not specify this failure-and-copy contract.
